notes: Crawler names, purposes, and robots.txt behavior are mutable platform facts. Recheck every source against current official documentation before a real audit.
A robots.txt Allow result is only a path-access rule result. It does not guarantee crawling, indexing, ranking, inclusion in an answer, or citation.
GPTBot is documented for potential foundation-model training; it is not treated as the ChatGPT Search crawler. OAI-SearchBot is evaluated separately for ChatGPT Search.
Google-Extended is intentionally not represented as a Google Search indexing control.

crawlers.purpose: Generic crawler product token used by Google Search for its smartphone and desktop crawlers.
Google Search mobile crawler; official documentation says it obeys the same Googlebot robots.txt product token as the desktop crawler.
crawlers.notes: Do not evaluate this as a separate Googlebot-Smartphone robots.txt token.

crawlers.purpose: Automatic crawler used to surface websites in ChatGPT search features.
Crawler for content that may be used to make OpenAI generative AI foundation models more useful and safe, including potential training use.
crawlers.notes: GPTBot is not the ChatGPT Search crawler; evaluate OAI-SearchBot separately.

crawlers.purpose: User-initiated web fetches for certain actions in ChatGPT and Custom GPTs; not an automatic web crawler and not the Search inclusion control.
crawlers.notes: Official documentation says robots.txt rules may not apply to these user-initiated requests.

crawlers.purpose: Crawler used by Anthropic to navigate and analyze web content to improve search result quality.
Crawler for public web content that could potentially contribute to Anthropic model training.
Retrieves web content at a Claude user's direction in response to a user query.
Crawler designed to surface and link websites in Perplexity search results; official documentation says it is not used to crawl for foundation-model training.
